https://telex.hu/after/2026/08/02/vincen.text: Menü Kereső Meghalt Vincent Pastore, a Maffiózók színésze After Nagy Nikoletta 80 éves korában meghalt Vincent Pastore amerikai színész, aki Salvatore „Big Pussy” Bonpensierót alakította a Maffiózók (The Sopranos) című sorozatban, írja a BBC . Sajtóértesülések szerint Pastore-t a Bronxbn található otthonában találták meg, és semmi nem utal idegenkezűségre. A Maffiózókban Pastore Tony Soprano legjobb barátját játszotta, aki végül az FBI informátora lett. Karakterének halála a második évad egyik legemlékezetesebb történetszála volt. Pastore 1946-ban született a New York-i Bronxban. A vietnámi háború idején belépett az amerikai haditengerészethez, majd később színészi karrierbe kezdett. Játszott a Nagymenőkben (Goodfellas) és a Carlito útjában (Carlito's Way), majd az Esküdt ellenségek, a General Hospital és a Hawaii Five-O sorozatokban is feltűnt. Karrierje igazi áttörést a Maffiózók hozta meg neki, ebben a karakterét a sorozat második évadában kiírták, Pastore mégis mind a hat évadban szerepelt. Kövess minket Facebookon is! Követem! https://telex.hu/sport/2026/08/11/kozak-.text: Menü Kereső Még célfotóval is alig lehetett eldönteni, hogy ki nyerte a női 100 gátat az Eb-n Sport Pia Skrzyszowska és Nadine Visser között egy ezredmásodperc döntött 100 gáton – Fotó: Martin Rickett / Getty Images Fehér János Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Célfotóval a holland Nadine Vissert hozták ki 100 méteres gátfutás győztesének a birminghami atlétikai Európa-bajnokságon, a zsűri szerint a Pia Skrzyszowskával századra ugyanannyit, 12,67 másodpercet futottak, de a holland egy ezreddel gyorsabb volt. Kozák Luca az ötödik lett a döntőben. A rajtot Skrzyszowska kapta el jobban, de a holland felzárkózott mellé, és mintha egymás árnyékai lettek volna, úgy haladtak a cél felé. A befutójuk után sokáig nem közölték az időeredményeket, a két atléta egymást átölelve várták az eredményeket, amik végül Vissernek kedveztek. Kozák Luca rajtja nem sikerült túl jól, de az utolsó húsz méteren a nyolcadik helyről fel tudott futni az ötödikre. Kozák az Eb-n kiemelt versenyző volt, így nem kellett futnia az előfutamban, egyből a legjobb 24 között kezdhetett. Az elődöntőjében övé volt a második legjobb nevezési idő, de sikerült felülírnia a papírformát. Nem kapta el igazán jól a rajtot, de jó ritmust talált, és a táv második felétől méterről méterre jött fel, és befogta az ellenfeleit, majd a célba már ő érkezett elsőként, néhány ezredmásodperccel megelőzte a belga Yanla Ndjip-Nyemecket is, és biztosan jutott a nyolcas döntőbe. Kozák kiemelkedő eredményét még a 2022-es Európa-bajnokságon érte el, akkor ezüstérmet szerzett. Idén újra kiemelkedő formába kerül, előbb 12,66 majd 12,59 másodpercre vitte le az országos csúcsot. Utóbbit szűk egy hónappal ezelőtt érte el a budapesti Gyulai Memorialon. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Kövess minket Facebookon is! Követem! (DSC) Daytona State College culinary student Cezar Nita has been selected as one of 220 Phi Theta Kappa members nationwide to receive a 2026 Coca-Cola Leaders of Promise Scholarship. For the recognition, he will also receive a $1,000 award. The Coca-Cola Leaders of Promise Scholarship Program helps new Phi Theta Kappa members offset educational expenses while pursuing associate degrees. Recipients are selected based on academic achievement, community service and leadership potential, and are encouraged to take leadership roles in Society programs. “Research shows that Phi Theta Kappa members are four times more likely to complete a college degree than their peers,” said Amanda Karpinski Gorman, Executive Director of the Phi Theta Kappa Foundation. “The Leaders of Promise Scholarships recognize students for what they have achieved already and assure that financial need isn’t an obstacle to achieving their academic goals.” A native of Craiova, Romania, Nita was living in New Hampshire and looking for opportunities to improve his English and study culinary arts. “I discovered Daytona State and was drawn to its Culinary Management program,” Nita said. “A recommendation from a chef I knew further confirmed my decision.”﻿ ﻿ Nita enrolled in the culinary program in Fall 2025 and is on track to graduate in 2027. “I’ve volunteered at school and culinary events, assisting with setup, service and guest experience,” he said. “I enjoy hospitality because it goes beyond food. It’s about creating memorable experiences and making guests feel genuinely cared for. ﻿ ﻿ “After graduation I plan to continue learning, grow as a chef and eventually build my own brand. Above all, I want to keep learning, cooking and pushing myself to grow in this career.” The Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation provides funding for the scholarships, with a portion earmarked for members who are veterans or active members of the United States military. Additional donations to the Phi Theta Kappa Foundation support multiple Global Leaders of Promise Scholarships earmarked for international students. “The Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation has a long history of providing financial assistance to outstanding students at community colleges,” said Jane Hale Paulsen, President of the Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation. “We are proud to partner with Phi Theta Kappa to make it possible for more deserving students to achieve their educational goals and support tomorrow’s leaders of the global community.” The funds provided by the Coca-Cola Scholars Foundation not only aid college completion but also give students the opportunity to engage in Society programs and develop leadership skills to become future leaders in their communities. https://www.dw.com/en/as-global-crises-g.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MYVI NGOs took to the street outside the chancellery to demonstrate against cutting development aid Image: Giulia Saudelli/DW Advertisement German Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan opened her speech in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, with a litany of catastrophes and suffering: floods in Nepal , heat waves, forests engulfed in flames, rivers running dry, and crop failures caused by drought. "Millions of people are facing hunger," said Radovan, of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD). "And one thing is clear: The climate crisis is threatening the entire world. No country can tackle it alone." Radovan opened the debate on the federal government's proposed 2027 budget for her ministry with a stark assessment. The budget is set to shrink for the fifth consecutive year, falling from just over €10 billion to just under €9.5 billion ($10.9 billion). In 2022, it stood at nearly €14 billion, meaning that the ministry's budget has been reduced by roughly one-third over the past half decade. Fighting to end suffering in Africa's conflict zones To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video How does this sharp decline square with the dramatic picture painted by Germany's development minister? She pointed to a strategy she unveiled in January , when she declared that "development policy will become an even more important pillar of German security, alongside diplomacy and defense." Funding for humanitarian aid stagnates Aid organizations reacted skeptically to this policy shift when it was first announced, and their concerns have deepened in light of the latest funding cuts. "The renewed reductions in funding for international cooperation are further exacerbating an already critical situation," said Michael Herbst of VENRO , the umbrella organization representing around 150 development and humanitarian NGOs. Herbst criticized the stagnant budget for humanitarian aid administered by the German Foreign Office. While it exceeded €3 billion in 2022, it has remained at just €1 billion since 2025. In light of worsening global crises, VENRO is calling for a change of course. "Next year, we will need to invest more in combating hunger because the conflict involving Iran and the dry summer are expected to trigger a sharp decline in agricultural yields," Herbst said, explaining the organization's demand for substantially higher funding. Ten million people left without assistance The impact of the cuts is already clearly visible, according to VENRO. A survey of its member organizations found that the number of funded projects is declining significantly. "Our sample of 34 organizations shows that, among these organizations alone, more than ten million fewer people are being reached with assistance." "And many local partner organizations, which are indispensable to effective development cooperation and humanitarian assistance, are no longer able to operate," Herbst said. He added that the full impact of these far-reaching cuts is unlikely to become apparent for another three to four years. A 'debt brake' exemption for development? The federal government's belt-tightening across virtually all ministries is a consequence of the Zeitenwende announced by 2022 Chancellor Olaf Scholz (SPD) in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine . Since then, Germany has embarked on a major military buildup, increasing its defense budget year after year, while nearly all other ministries have had to make do with significantly less funding. Herbst, a member of VENRO's executive board, is calling on the Bundestag to exempt both development cooperation and humanitarian assistance from Germany's "debt brake." "After all, exceptions have already been made for the modernization of the Bundeswehr and for military aid to Ukraine," he said. Herbst said an exemption would enable Germany to once again assume greater responsibility on the international stage. Germany's Radovan warns SDGs unlikely to be met by 2030 To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Less money, less impact? Jamila Schäfer, a member of parliament from the opposition Green Party , made a similar argument during the Bundestag debate on the Development Ministry's budget. Climate action and development cooperation, she argued, are not acts of charity but are firmly in Germany's own interest. "Germany must invest in its defense capabilities, but security is not created through investments in the defense budget alone," Schäfer said. "Those who strengthen military security while cutting support for international stability have a blind spot in their security policy." Nicolas Zippelius, a lawmaker from the governing center-right conservative alliance, the Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU), sees the ongoing cuts to development spending differently. In his view, every ministry must contribute to consolidating the federal budget. "Less money does not necessarily mean a smaller impact. Instead, it should encourage us to focus more clearly on priorities and critically review existing structures." Zippelius dismisses demands to exempt the Development Ministry from Germany's debt brake. "The key question is whether every euro spent is directed to where it can make the greatest difference." The Christian Democrat argues that success in development cooperation, as in other areas of policy, should be judged not by the size of the budget but by the impact it achieves. German Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan in Kenya To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The case for more prevention Jan Sebastian Friedrich-Rust, who heads the humanitarian and development aid organization Action Against Hunger , has a very different view. "The cuts planned for the 2027 budget are short-sighted and dangerous. As a result, up to 22.6 million people worldwide could die by 2030," he said in a written statement to DW. Cuts to development cooperation and humanitarian aid are also fiscally short-sighted, Friedrich-Rust said. "Hunger, crises and instability generate long-term costs that far exceed the cost of prevention. Those who cut spending today are merely postponing the bill and ultimately making it much more expensive," he warned. To underscore its concerns, the Action Against Hunger alliance delivered a petition to the leaders of the governing coalition of SPD and CDU/CSU parliamentary groups on the eve of the Bundestag's budget debate. About 100,000 people added their names to the appeal, titled "Don't Balance the Budget at the Expense of Solidarity: Strengthen International Aid!" This article was originally written in German. https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: The park confirmed the tiger, named Altai, was ‘safe and well and will not be euthanised’ after the incident. Photograph: Yorkshire Wildlife Park/SWNS View image in fullscreen The park confirmed the tiger, named Altai, was ‘safe and well and will not be euthanised’ after the incident. Photograph: Yorkshire Wildlife Park/SWNS Yorkshire Wildlife park confirms tiger will not be euthanised after man mauled to death Ed Miliband, whose constituency includes the park, offers ‘deepest condolences’ to family of visitor who entered enclosure on Saturday Neha Gohil Sun 11 Oct 2026 09.48 EDT Last modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 11.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A wildlife park in Yorkshire has confirmed the tiger that mauled to death a man who entered its enclosure will not be euthanised. A man, who has not yet been named, was seen entering a tiger enclosure at the Yorkshire Wildlife Park, located near Doncaster , before police were called at 1.35pm on Saturday. South Yorkshire police said the tiger “subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injury” and despite the efforts of emergency services, the man was pronounced dead at the scene. In a statement on Sunday, the wildlife park thanked those who had expressed concern after the “tragic incident” and said their “thoughts and heartfelt sympathies” remained with the family of the man who lost his life. “The park will be closed today and the staff team who were deeply affected by events will receive specialist support,” the statement read. The park also confirmed that the tiger, named Altai, was “safe and well and will not be euthanised” after the incident. View image in fullscreen Yorkshire Wildlife Park was closed on Sunday. Photograph: Charley Atkins/SWNS The foreign secretary and MP for Doncaster North, Ed Miliband , said he was “deeply saddened” and sent his “thoughts and deepest condolences to the family of the individual who died”. “I am very grateful to the emergency services and staff of the park who responded,” Miliband added. One visitor at the park, Marie Miller, wrote in a Facebook post that she had seen the man before the incident and he was “happily enjoying” his visit. Miller said the man had asked a stranger to take a picture of him. “The man who I saw on the bridge with his earpods in dancing was happily enjoying seeing the tiger,” the post read. “He asked a total stranger to take a picture of him with the tiger in the background.” Another visitor, who did not want to be identified, told the South West News Service that it was “frightening and confusing” when the park was evacuated after the incident. She said: “At first, we were all scared and confused because we had no idea what was going on. Different routes had been closed off, and staff were positioned around the park directing visitors where to go. “The scariest part was not knowing what was happening.” The visitor said she heard people saying the man was 22, but was unable to confirm this. “As we walked past the police near the tiger enclosure, we saw officers surrounding a young man in the tiger enclosure,” she said. “We saw an air ambulance outside the park, although, from what we observed, it didn’t take anyone away.” South Yorkshire police said the man’s family was made aware of the incident on Saturday and were being supported by specialist officers. The force has encouraged people not to share videos of the incident that have been circulating online. Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009, with the Land of the Tigers attraction opening in 2011. The attraction is on a purpose-built 2-acre reserve for Amur tigers, an endangered subspecies with about 500 left in the wild. https://www.dw.com/en/werner-holzer-priz.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PRqO Prefer DW on Google Jaafar Abdul Karim (left) and Katja Gloger were the proud winners of the award for outstanding international journalism Image: Sven Moschitz Advertisement At a time when press freedom is under pressure and international newsrooms are shrinking, the Werner Holzer Prize celebrates a profession that many consider indispensable to democracy: foreign correspondence. Presented in honor of Werner Holzer, the veteran reporter and former editor-in-chief of the German daily newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau , this year's award coincided with what would have been his 100th birthday. Holzer spent decades reporting from some of the world's most important hot spots and championing international journalism. At the award ceremony in Frankfurt's Römer, the city's historic town hall, Mayor Mike Josef recalled that fundamental rights such as freedom of speech and freedom of the press were first enshrined for all Germans by the Frankfurt Parliament in the nearby Paulskirche in 1848. Germany's public broadcasters under fire from far-right AfD To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The 2026 winners reflect the breadth and ambition of the award. First prize went to Katja Gloger, a veteran Russia correspondent who moved to Moscow in 1989 and accompanied Vladimir Putin during the early years of his presidency. In her recent nonfiction book, "The Failure: An Investigative Report of Germany's Russia Policy," Gloger and co-author Georg Mascolo offer a searing critique of the misjudgments and illusions that shaped German policy toward Russia for decades . Second prize was awarded to DW journalist and presenter Jaafar Abdul Karim. His talk show JaafarTalk reaches millions of viewers across the Arab world and in Germany. Whether in Tunis, Beirut or Cairo, Abdul Karim tackles subjects that are often considered taboo. A research grant went to freelance journalist Luise Land, whose current project explores why her German-Namibian family still owns extensive landholdings in Namibia today. By tracing that history, she examines the enduring legacy of the genocide against the Herero and Nama peoples by German colonial forces in the early 20th century. Call for more international coverage "Katja Gloger is one of the leading foreign policy reporters. For decades, she has been among the foremost experts on Russia and speaks out on uncomfortable truths," the jury stated on Friday, explaining its decision to honor Gloger. "Like almost no one else, she has gained access to the very heart of the Kremlin's power elite — from Mikhail Gorbachev to Vladimir Putin." At the prize-giving ceremony, Gloger delivered a passionate plea for more journalism — and more international coverage — in the German press. "We must defend trustworthy, reliable and fact-based journalism with everything in our power," she said. Why press freedom matters to everyone, not just journalists To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Gloger worked for Reporters Without Borders for 12 years. "The latest rankings show that only one in 100 people can get their information from free, independent journalism and a free, independent press . That shows what's at stake," she said. The prize winner also said she would dedicate the award to journalists in exile and to her colleagues at Novaya Gazeta , the independent Russian newspaper long known for its critical reporting on the Kremlin. Earlier this week, the paper was forced to shut down its operations in Russia and leave its Moscow newsroom . Belief in the power of dialogue In his acceptance speech, Jaafar Abdul Karim said journalism has become more challenging and exhausting than ever. The DW host spoke of hatred and incitement, attacks and threats, both online and offline, in the regions he reports on as well as in Germany . Such pressure, he said, takes a personal toll — yet giving up is not an option. "When I listen to my heart, I know I have to keep going," he said. The answer, he argued, is a form of journalism that fosters dialogue, embraces multiple perspectives and helps bridge divides rather than deepen them. "I firmly believe in the power of dialogue, today more than ever. That's why we must talk to one another. Even when it gets difficult. Even when we disagree. Or perhaps precisely because of that," he said. 'When everyone jumps to conclusions, we need journalists who ask questions first,' said DW's Jaafar Abdul Karim Image: Sven Moschitz Listening doesn't mean agreeing, and understanding doesn't mean being in agreement. "Especially now, in times of polarization, when those who believe they're always right are often the loudest, we as journalists have a special responsibility. When everyone is just shouting into their own bubbles or communities, we need journalists who connect these bubbles with one another," he said. The jury praised Abdul Karim for creating programs at DW that reach millions of young people across the Arab world and in Germany. "His journalism fosters dialogue between countries, between generations, and between religions. He has set new standards," the jury stated. So far in 2026, JaafarTalk has already garnered more than 1.1 billion views across all platforms, and its community has grown to more than 9 million followers. Its motto: "Diversity fosters dialogue." "We need fact-based journalism that promotes dialogue and reflects the diversity of our society," Abdul Karim stressed. "By that, I mean an honest and open dialogue in which we do not look away or remain silent. On the contrary, we must take a clear stand against racism , antisemitism , Islamophobia , discrimination , sexism , and hate speech — no matter which side they come from." This article was originally written in German. https://hvg.hu/vilag/20261115_esztorszag.text: A balti állam külügyminisztere szerint egyértelmű bizonyítékok támasztják alá, hogy a GRU szabotázsakciót rendelt el egy észt védelmi ipari vállalat ellen. Észtország az orosz határ lezárását tervezi december 1-jétől - közölte vasárnap Margus Tsahkna, a balti ország külügyminisztere ( képünkön ). Following clear evidence that Russia’s military intelligence service GRU, ordered a sabotage attack against an Estonian defence industry company, Estonia will close all Estonian-Russian border crossing points as of 1 December.Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences. Attempts to intimidate, destabilise, or undermine our security will not go unanswered.Closing the border crossings will reduce Russia’s ability to conduct hostile activities in Estonia and strengthen our efforts to prevent sanctions circumvention.I have informed my Finnish, Latvian, and Lithuanian counterparts of this decision. Tsahkna az X-en arról számolt be, hogy Tallinn tájékoztatta Finnországot, Lettországot és Litvániát szándékáról, hogy december elejétől lezárja a határátkelőket. Igor Taro észt belügyminiszter pedig nem sokkal korábban közölte, hogy a határ lezárásáról szóló döntést a jövő héten fogja elfogadni a kabinet. A külügyminiszter közlése szerint azután hozták meg a döntést, hogy „egyértelmű bizonyítékok támasztják alá, hogy az orosz katonai hírszerző szolgálat, a GRU szabotázsakciót rendelt el egy észt védelmi ipari vállalat ellen”. Egy korábbi posztjában azt írta, hogy az észt Belbiztonsági Szolgálat erősítette meg, hogy a november 14-én az észt Threod Systems ellen elkövetett, sikertelen gyújtogatási kísérletet a GRU rendelte el. Az észt hatóságok vasárnap adtak hírt arról, hogy nyolc gyanúsítottat vettek őrizetbe a Threod Systems dróngyártó vállalat épülete elleni gyújtogatás ügyében. Astrid Asi észt főügyész szerint a szombat kora reggeli órákban történt incidenst a cég biztonsági embereinek sikerült megakadályozniuk. Az érintettek közül öt ember ellen letartóztatási parancsot adtak ki. A cég egyebek között Ukrajna számára is gyárt felderítő, illetve harci drónokat. Margo Palloson, az észt biztonsági szolgálat vezetője szerint az elkövetők egy betört ablakon keresztül próbáltak gyúlékony folyadékot beönteni és felgyújtani. Szerinte ha minden a támadók tervei szerint alakult volna, akkor jelentős károk is keletkezhettek volna. „Oroszországnak tisztában kell lennie azzal, hogy az Észtország ellen irányuló ellenséges cselekmények következményekkel járnak. A megfélemlítésre, a destabilizálásra vagy a biztonságunk aláásására irányuló kísérletek nem maradnak válasz nélkül” - közölte Margus Tsahkna. A külügyminiszter szerint a határátkelőhelyek lezárása csökkenti Oroszország képességét arra, hogy ellenséges tevékenységeket folytasson Észtországban, és megerősíti a szankciók kijátszásának megakadályozására irányuló erőfeszítéseket is. Az intézkedés nem példa nélküli, 2024-ben Finnország is lezárta a határát Oroszországgal, ami azóta is hatályban van. Madáretetőben is találtak bankjegyeket az NVVH nyomozói. Az elnök szerint „senkinek az óvodai jele” nincs a megtalált hat és félmilliárdon, majd eldől, hogy kié volt. A húsleves és a rántott hús sokaknak ismerős kiindulópont, de az ország étkezési kultúrája jóval sokszínűbb annál, mint amit a klasszikus családi ebédről alkotott képünk sugall. Csaknem egy óráig keresték a routerrel dolgozó szakembert, mert papíron vezetik a munkanaplót.

https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/mapa.text: O puternică explozie a fost auzită miercuri dimineaţă la Riad de către jurnalişti ai AFP, cu câteva minute înainte de anunţul interceptării unei rachete trase de rebelii houthi din Yemen către capitala saudită şi a unei alte rachete în sudul ţării, scrie Agerpres. „Suflul exploziei a deschis uşile tuturor camerelor, iar lumina s-a stins pentru scurt timp”, a povestit pentru AFP o locuitoare din Riad care a dorit să îşi păstreze anonimatul, în timp ce un alt rezident a spus că a simţit „geamurile vibrând”. Regatul este vizat cu regularitate de către rebelii houthi pro-iranieni de la reluarea ostilităţilor în Yemenul vecin. Însă populaţia nu a primit miercuri dimineaţă niciun mesaj de alertă privind un posibil pericol, aşa cum se întâmplă de obicei. Locul exploziei de dimineaţă nu a fost identificat, dar martorii au declarat pentru AFP că au văzut fum în apropierea aeroportului din Riad, care a fost deja lovit de mai multe ori. Câteva minute mai târziu, coaliţia condusă de Arabia Saudită, care sprijină din 2015 guvernul yemenit împotriva rebelilor houthi, a anunţat pe X că a interceptat o rachetă de croazieră lansată de această mişcare în direcţia capitalei. O altă rachetă a fost interceptată mai devreme, potrivit aceleiaşi surse. În cursul serii, coaliţia a raportat noi interceptări a două drone houthi, una în regiunea Riad şi cealaltă în sudul regatului. Cu puţin timp înainte, apărarea civilă emisese o alertă, ridicată rapid, care semnala un „pericol” în guvernoratul Sharurah, în sud. Purtătorul de cuvânt militar al rebelilor houthi, Yahya Saree, a afirmat în cursul serii că mişcarea a vizat în cursul zilei aeroportul internaţional din Riad, centrul financiar al capitalei, precum şi o bază aeriană şi o „ţintă sensibilă” în regiunea Jizan, ambele în sudul regatului, revendicând operaţiuni desfăşurate cu succes. Conflictul din Yemen a izbucnit în 2014 când rebelii houthi au lansat o ofensivă împotriva forţelor guvernamentale şi au preluat controlul asupra unor părţi întinse din nordul ţării, inclusiv asupra capitalei Sanaa. Reluarea acestuia în iulie, după patru ani de acalmie, a deschis un nou front în războiul din Orientul Mijlociu. Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News
